title_en: Gao Lizhen (Third Party) v. Yong'an Yancheng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., Zheng Yaonan, and Far East (Xiamen) Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — third-party revocation action
ruling_gist_en: Although a third party that is an ordinary creditor generally does not have a cause of action for a third-party revocation action based on creditor's rights, if the disposition of the debtor's property confirmed by an effective judgment meets the conditions for the right of revocation under Article 74 of the Contract Law, then the creditor who enjoys the statutory right of revocation has a legal interest in the outcome of the case concerning that effective judgment, and thus has standing as a plaintiff to bring a third-party revocation action as a third party without independent claim.

full_text_en:
Yong'an Yancheng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. v. Zheng Yaonan, Far East (Xiamen) Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., and Third Party Gao Lizhen — third party revocation action

Ruling Summary

A third party who is an ordinary creditor generally does not have a cause of action to file a third party revocation action based on creditor's rights. However, if the property disposition of the debtor confirmed by an effective judgment meets the conditions for a revocatory right under Article 74 of the Contract Law, then the creditor who enjoys such revocatory right has a legal interest in the outcome of the case of that effective judgment, and thus qualifies as a plaintiff with the standing to file a third party revocation action as a third party without independent claims.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

Civil Final No. 885 (2017) of the Supreme People's Court

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Yong'an Yancheng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 35, Wusi Road, Yong'an City, Fujian Province.

Legal Representative: Lei Yuansi, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Lijian, lawyer of Fujian Golden Bay Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Xie Guangdong, lawyer of Fujian Golden Bay Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Zheng Yaonan, resident of the Taiwan Region, male, born on November 28, 1949, residing in Zhongzheng District, Taipei City, Taiwan Region.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Far East (Xiamen) Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. Domicile: Units C and D, 13/F, Zhenye Building, Hubin North Road, Siming District, Xiamen City, Fujian Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Qiongyue, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Wang Guowen, lawyer of Fujian Yinghe Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liu Yan, lawyer of Fujian Yinghe Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Gao Lizhen, resident of the Taiwan Region, female, born on December 6, 1971, residing in Nantun District, Taichung City, Taiwan Region.

Agent ad litem: Luo Changshui, lawyer of Fujian Tianheng United Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Lyu Liangyi, lawyer of Fujian Tianheng United Law Firm.

The appellant, Yong'an Yancheng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yancheng Company), appealed to this Court against the civil ruling of the Fujian High People's Court (2016) Min Min Che No. 6 in a case of third party revocation action with the respondents Zheng Yaonan and Far East (Xiamen) Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Far East Xiamen Company) and the third party at first instance Gao Lizhen. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and conducted a public hearing. The agents ad litem of the appellant Yancheng Company, Zhang Lijian and Xie Guangdong, the agent ad litem of the respondent Far East Xiamen Company, Liu Yan, and the agent ad litem of the third party at first instance, Gao Lizhen, Lyu Liangyi, appeared before the court. The respondent Zheng Yaonan, after being served with summons by this Court, did not appear before the court. This case has now been concluded.

Yancheng Company appealed requesting: 1. To set aside the civil ruling of the Fujian High People's Court (2016) Min Min Che No. 6; and 2. To instruct the Fujian High People's Court to conduct substantive trial of this case in accordance with the law. Facts and reasons: (1) Yancheng Company is a bankruptcy creditor of Far East Xiamen Company. Gao Lizhen declared a huge amount of claims based on the civil mediation (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Mediation) of Case No. (2003) Min Min Chu Zi No. 2, Zheng Yaonan v. Far East Xiamen Company — dispute over loan (hereinafter referred to as Case No. 2), which is causing a significant adverse impact on the realization of Yancheng Company's bankruptcy claims. Case No. 2 is a fraudulent lawsuit in which the parties colluded maliciously to transfer assets, affecting the interests of bankruptcy creditors. Yancheng Company has an obvious legal interest in the outcome of Case No. 2. Therefore, Yancheng Company, as a third party without independent claims in Case No. 2, has the standing to file this lawsuit. The first instance court's finding that Yancheng Company "has no legal interest in the debt involved in the loan dispute between Zheng Yaonan and Far East Xiamen Company" is clearly erroneous. (2) As a bankruptcy creditor of Far East Xiamen Company, Yancheng Company could only know that its civil rights and interests were harmed upon receiving notice from the bankruptcy administrator confirming that Far East Xiamen Company had a loan debt. Therefore, the statute of limitations for this case should run from the date Yancheng Company received the notice of confirmation of such loan debt from the bankruptcy administrator, i.e., from August 16, 2016. Yancheng Company filed this lawsuit on September 12 of the same year, which did not exceed the six-month statutory period for a third party revocation action. (3) The personal complaint behavior of Lei Yuansi representing Far East Xiamen Company does not equate to Yancheng Company knowing or being able to know that its civil rights and interests were harmed before the bankruptcy. The first instance court's determination that Yancheng Company knew or could have known that its rights were harmed based on Lei Yuansi's personal behavior representing Far East Xiamen Company is clearly erroneous in logic and fact. (4) A people's court has the responsibility to initiate error correction procedures in accordance with the law for judgments that have been found to be truly erroneous. This case should be subjected to substantive trial to uphold the dignity of the law and protect the lawful rights and interests of the parties and all bankruptcy creditors. (5) A people's court should form a collegial panel to hold a hearing in a third party revocation action case. The first instance court did not hold a hearing, and the procedure and ruling were erroneous. The first instance court failed to ascertain the basic facts of the fraudulent lawsuit in Case No. 2 and the malicious collusion between the parties, and simply concluded that Yancheng Company had no legal interest in Case No. 2, which lacks factual basis. In summary, Yancheng Company, as a creditor in the bankruptcy case, fully meets the qualifications and conditions for filing a third party revocation action. The first instance court made errors in both fact-finding and application of law, which should be corrected in accordance with the law.

Zheng Yaonan submitted a written defense opinion, stating that the first instance ruling had clear findings of fact and correct application of law. (1) Yancheng Company is not a proper party in this case, and the first instance court's finding of fact is correct. According to the principle of privity of contract, Case No. 2 is a private lending dispute between Zheng Yaonan and Far East Xiamen Company. Whether Far East Xiamen Company has other creditors is not within the scope of review in that case, and there is no third party who must participate in the proceedings. Yancheng Company is not a third party in that case. (2) Lei Yuansi, the legal representative of Yancheng Company, already knew about Case No. 2 as early as 2003 and filed a complaint against the Civil Mediation with the Fujian Provincial People's Procuratorate. Yancheng Company was fully aware of the entire process of that case but never exercised its rights conferred by law, such as filing a complaint with the procuratorate. This constitutes a dereliction of the exercise of rights. By the time it filed this lawsuit, the statutory period had already expired. (3) The Civil Mediation has already been reviewed by the Fujian High People's Court, and that case did not meet the conditions for initiating trial supervision proceedings. It is evident that the Civil Mediation does not contain any error in content. Yancheng Company's claims do not satisfy the conditions set forth in Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law). Even if the court accepts this case, Yancheng Company's claims cannot be sustained. (4) On April 8, 2015, Zheng Yaonan and the third party Gao Lizhen entered into a "Debt Transfer Agreement" for the transfer of all claims under the Civil Mediation to Gao Lizhen, and Far East Xiamen Company was notified accordingly. All civil rights and obligations under the Civil Mediation have been succeeded by Gao Lizhen. The lawsuit filed by Yancheng Company is irrelevant to Zheng Yaonan. In summary, the statutory period for Yancheng Company to file this third party revocation action has already expired, and Yancheng Company is not a proper party in this case. Zheng Yaonan requests that the court of second instance dismiss all of its appeal requests in accordance with the law.

Far East Xiamen Company argued that whether Yancheng Company meets the conditions for filing a third party revocation action should be determined by the court in accordance with the law.

Gao Lizhen stated: (1) Yancheng Company's claim that Case No. 2 involves malicious collusion and is a fraudulent lawsuit is supported by no evidence. The case of Zhang Qiongyue v. Far East Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hong Kong Far East Company) — dispute over loan contract, which Yancheng Company referred to, occurred after the filing of Case No. 2. It is the later case that should be reviewed by the court, not the legality of this case. (2) The first instance court dismissed Yancheng Company's action primarily on the ground that Yancheng Company lacked standing as a proper party. Such matters are within the scope of review that the court should conduct ex officio during the case filing process and do not require a formal hearing. The first instance procedure was not erroneous, and Yancheng Company's appeal grounds are untenable. Other opinions are the same as Zheng Yaonan's first, second, and third defense opinions.

Yancheng Company filed a lawsuit with the first instance court requesting: to set aside the Civil Mediation of the Fujian High People's Court (2003) Min Min Chu Zi No. 2.

The first instance court held that this case involves a third party revocation action. It must first examine from a procedural perspective whether Yancheng Company meets the conditions for filing a third party revocation action. (1) Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law provides: "Where a third party considers that it has an independent claim to the subject matter of the litigation between the parties, it has the right to bring an action. Where a third party does not have an independent claim to the subject matter of the litigation between the parties, but the outcome of the case has a legal interest for it, it may apply to participate in the proceedings, or the people's court may notify it to participate in the proceedings. If a people's court holds a third party liable for civil obligations, such third party shall have the litigation rights and obligations of a party. Where a third party mentioned in the preceding two paragraphs fails to participate in the proceedings for reasons not attributable to its own fault, but has evidence to prove that part or all of the contents of a legally effective judgment, ruling, or mediation are erroneous and that such errors harm its civil rights and interests, it may, within six months from the date it knows or should know that its civil rights and interests are harmed, file an action with the people's court that rendered the judgment, ruling, or mediation." Although Yancheng Company is a claimant of claims in the bankruptcy case of Far East Xiamen Company, it has no independent claim to the debts involved in Case No. 2, nor does it have a legal interest in the outcome of that case. Therefore, Yancheng Company is not a third party in Case No. 2. Pursuant to the above provision, Yancheng Company lacks standing to file a third party revocation action. (2) According to Article 292 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Judicial Interpretation of the Civil Procedure Law), which provides: "Where a third party files a revocation action against a legally effective judgment, ruling, or mediation, it shall file the action with the people's court that rendered the effective judgment, ruling, or mediation within six months from the date it knows or should know that its civil rights and interests are harmed." The period for filing a third party revocation action runs for six months from the date the third party knows or should know that its civil rights and interests are harmed, and this six-month period is a non-extendable period. Even if Yancheng Company had the standing to file a third party revocation action, it should have filed the action within six months from the date it knew or should have known that its civil rights and interests were harmed. According to the evidence submitted by Yancheng Company, Yancheng Company was established in 1992, Lei Yuansi became general manager on March 9, 1995, and became chairman of the board on November 11, 1996. In July 2003, Lei Yuansi filed a complaint with the Fujian High People's Court and the Fujian Provincial People's Procuratorate regarding Case No. 2. It can be determined that the date Yancheng Company knew or should have known that its civil rights and interests were harmed was when its legal representative Lei Yuansi filed the complaint. Considering that the third party revocation action is a system newly established after the amendment of the Civil Procedure Law in 2012, even if the six-month period is calculated from the date of implementation on January 1, 2013, Yancheng Company has already exceeded the statutory period for filing a third party revocation action.

The first instance court, in accordance with Article 56 and Article 154, Paragraph 1, Item 3 of the Civil Procedure Law and Article 292 of the Judicial Interpretation of the Civil Procedure Law, ruled to dismiss Yancheng Company's action.

This Court finds through trial that, to prove that it meets the conditions and standing for filing this third party revocation action, Yancheng Company submitted to the first instance court evidence materials showing relevant circumstances in the following eight aspects.

I. The Civil Mediation of Case No. 2 of the Fujian High People's Court shows that the court accepted Case No. 2 on May 12, 2003, i.e., Zheng Yaonan v. Far East Xiamen Company — dispute over loan, and made the Civil Mediation on June 2 of the same year, confirming the following agreement voluntarily reached by the parties: (1) The parties confirmed that, as of April 10, 2003, Far East Xiamen Company owed Zheng Yaonan principal amounts of USD 3,306,757.78 and HKD 3,051,046 (equivalent to a total of RMB 31,245,079.22), and interest amounts of USD 9,735,293.7 and HKD 8,870,568.13 (equivalent to a total of RMB 91,884,448.5). The total amount of principal and interest owed is equivalent to RMB 123,129,527.72. Zheng Yaonan voluntarily waived interest after April 11, 2003. (2) Far East Xiamen Company agreed to repay the aforementioned principal and interest in the following manner: 1. Within two days from the effective date of this mediation, Far East Xiamen Company shall repay Zheng Yaonan RMB 50,000,000; 2. Before July 1, 2003, Far East Xiamen Company shall repay Zheng Yaonan RMB 20,000,000; 3. Within the 12 months from August 1, 2003 to July 31, 2004, Far East Xiamen Company shall repay Zheng Yaonan RMB 4,000,000 before the 30th of each month; 4. Before October 31, 2005, Far East Xiamen Company shall repay the remaining amount of RMB 5,129,527.72 to Zheng Yaonan. (3) If Far East Xiamen Company fails to repay any installment as agreed, Zheng Yaonan has the right to demand accelerated repayment of all outstanding portions. (4) The case acceptance fee of RMB 625,657.6 shall be borne by Far East Xiamen Company. Given that Zheng Yaonan has prepaid it, Far East Xiamen Company shall pay this amount to Zheng Yaonan within two days from the effective date of this mediation.

II. The "Transfer Letter of Criminal Clues" (2003) Min Min Jian Zi No. 149 issued by the Fujian High People's Court to the Fujian Provincial Public Security Department on October 24, 2003 states: There are suspicious points in the loan relationship between Zheng Yaonan and Zhang Qiongyue that may involve embezzlement of property. 1. From 1994 to 1997, Zheng Yaonan made 12 large loans to Far East Xiamen Company. Among them, five promissory notes dated August 25, 1994, August 29, 1994, September 2, 1994, and January 10, 1995, had a loan term of one year each. However, Far East Xiamen Company failed to repay for many years after the maturity date, and Zheng Yaonan did not demand repayment until 2003. 2. Far East Xiamen Company was established on October 5, 1994, but four promissory notes dated August 25, 1994, August 29, 1994, and September 2, 1994 were written on Far East Xiamen Company's letterhead paper before its establishment. 3. Far East Xiamen Company's balance sheets, income statements, profit distribution statements, cash flow statements, statements of changes in financial position, and audit reports for previous years did not record the huge loans between Far East Xiamen Company and Zheng Yaonan. 4. Six bank transfer vouchers (slips) and one foreign exchange transaction notice, which should have been archived in Far East Xiamen Company's financial records, were copied by Zheng Yaonan and submitted as evidence to support his claim. 5. Since Far East Xiamen Company admitted the fact of borrowing from Zheng Yaonan and was willing to repay, why did the parties resort to legal proceedings to resolve the loan dispute? In summary, we believe that Zheng Yaonan and Zhang Qiongyue of Far East Xiamen Company are suspected of malicious collusion, embezzling the property of Far East Xiamen Company, and thereby harming the lawful rights and interests of Hong Kong Far East Company. At the same time, considering that the case of Zheng Yaonan v. Far East Xiamen Company — dispute over loan heard by our court complies with legal provisions in both trial procedure and substantive handling, it is not appropriate to directly initiate trial supervision proceedings. Therefore, in accordance with Article 10 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Related to the Handling of Economic Disputes Involving Economic Crimes (2000), which provides: "Where a people's court, during the trial of an economic dispute case, discovers clues or materials of economic crimes that are connected to the case but are not the same legal relationship, it shall transfer such clues or materials to the relevant public security authority for investigation and handling in accordance with the law," we hereby transfer the above clues and suspicions to your department for investigation and handling in accordance with the law.

III. A written notice issued by the Civil Administrative Procuratorial Department of the Fujian Provincial People's Procuratorate to Lei Yuansi on November 10, 2003 states: You filed a complaint with our procuratorate against the Civil Mediation of Case No. 2 of the Fujian High People's Court in the case of Zheng Yaonan v. Far East Xiamen Company — dispute over loan contract. On August 19, 2003, our procuratorate issued a "Procuratorial Recommendation" (2003) Min Min Jian No. 2 to the Fujian High People's Court, recommending that the case be retried in accordance with the law. The Fujian High People's Court replied to our procuratorate on October 24, 2003, stating that it had reviewed the case and, in accordance with the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Related to the Handling of Economic Disputes Involving Economic Crimes, had transferred the criminal clues of Far East Xiamen Company's legal representative Zhang Qiongyue being suspected of malicious collusion with Zheng Yaonan to embezzle the assets of Far East Xiamen Company to the Fujian Provincial Public Security Department for investigation.

IV. A notarial certificate (2015) Xia Zheng Nei Zi No. 12164 issued by the Xiamen Notary Public Office, Fujian Province on April 8, 2015 shows that on the same day the certificate was issued, Zheng Yaonan and Gao Lizhen entered into a "Debt Transfer Agreement," which states that the parties, through negotiation, reached the following terms: (1) Now, because the debt issue of Far East Xiamen Company has not been resolved for a long time, and Zheng Yaonan cannot reside in Xiamen for an extended period, he hereby transfers all his claims under the Civil Mediation to Gao Lizhen. From the date of signing this agreement, all rights related to such claims shall be exercised by Gao Lizhen, and Zheng Yaonan shall have no involvement. All legal actions required for the exercise of the claims and related expenses shall also be borne by Gao Lizhen, and Zheng Yaonan shall have no involvement; (2) As of the date of signing this agreement, the consideration for the transfer of the claims has been fully paid; (3) After the signing of this agreement, Gao Lizhen may, in her own name, directly claim from Far East Xiamen Company all rights and interests under the aforesaid claims (including but not limited to principal, interest, liquidated damages, etc.) and enjoy lawful creditor's rights. A statement issued by Far East Xiamen Company to Zheng Yaonan and Gao Lizhen on April 10 shows that it confirmed receipt of the above notarial certificate, acknowledged that it was aware of the transfer of the claims of Zheng Yaonan against Far East Xiamen Company to Gao Lizhen, and that Gao Lizhen had become a creditor of Far East Xiamen Company and would repay debts to Gao Lizhen in accordance with the law.

V. A civil ruling (2015) Xia Min Po Zi No. 6 issued by the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court, Fujian Province on December 21, 2015 shows that the court ruled to accept the bankruptcy liquidation application filed by the applicant Xiamen Kaibite Investment Co., Ltd. against the respondent Far East Xiamen Company, and appointed Fujian Yinghe Law Firm as the administrator of Far East Xiamen Company.

VI. The bankruptcy administrator of Far East Xiamen Company sent to Yancheng Company on March 15, 2016 the Notice [2015] Far East Bankruptcy Management Letter No. 8 entitled "Notice Regarding Informing Creditors of Far East Xiamen Company to Inspect the Documents for Creditor’s Rights Declaration" in the Bankruptcy Case of Far East (Xiamen) Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., which showed that the notice's subject line read "Regarding informing creditors of Far East Xiamen Company to inspect the materials for creditor’s rights declaration," and the content indicated that Fujian Yinghe Law Firm, as the bankruptcy administrator, had compiled the following statistics of the creditor’s rights declarations currently accepted: ...5. Yancheng Company declared RMB 14,158,920; 6. Gao Lizhen declared RMB 312,294,743.65; total RMB 725,856,487.91. The bankruptcy administrator had now scanned the materials for the creditor’s rights declared by the above creditors into electronic files for inspection by each creditor. For the protection of the creditors' own interests, if any creditor had objections to the creditor’s rights declared by others after inspecting the above materials, they should submit them in writing to the bankruptcy administrator before March 18. The notice was signed for by Zhang Lijian on March 15, 2016.

VII. The "Table of Creditor's Rights" (2015) Xiamen Civil Bankruptcy No. 6 prepared by Fujian Yinghe Law Firm on August 10, 2016, recorded that among the amounts of creditor’s rights declared by creditor Gao Lizhen on the grounds of a loan contract and classified as ordinary creditor’s rights, the original creditor’s rights amounted to RMB 123,755,185.32, and the accrued-interest creditor’s rights amounted to RMB 188,539,588.33, totaling RMB 312,294,743.65; among the amounts of creditor’s rights examined by the administrator, the original creditor’s rights were RMB 123,129,527.72, and the accrued-interest creditor’s rights were RMB 178,460,380.4, totaling RMB 301,589,908.12. Among the amounts of creditor’s rights declared by creditor Yancheng Company and classified as ordinary creditor’s rights, the original creditor’s rights were RMB 3,900,000, and the accrued-interest creditor’s rights were RMB 10,258,920, totaling RMB 14,158,920; among the amounts examined by the administrator, the original creditor’s rights were RMB 3,900,000, and the accrued-interest creditor’s rights were RMB 0, totaling RMB 3,900,000.

VIII. The certificate of legal representative of Yancheng Company showed that its legal representative was Lei Yuansi. The civil complaint in Case No. 2 filed by Zheng Yaonan against Far East Xiamen Company indicated that the legal representative of Far East Xiamen Company was Zhang Qiongyue. The civil judgment of the Supreme People's Court (2013) Min Si Zhong Zi No. 25 stated that Lei Yuansi and Zhang Qiongyue were both directors of Hong Kong Far East Company, each holding 50% of the company's shares; Far East Xiamen Company was a wholly-owned subsidiary established by Hong Kong Far East Company.

Opinion of the Court: The present case is a third-party revocation action brought by a third party who claims that the parties have maliciously colluded in litigation, thereby harming its interests. Because Zheng Yaonan and Gao Lizhen are residents of the Taiwan region, this case is a cross-strait civil dispute. All parties have no objection to the application of the law of mainland China by the court of first instance to resolve the dispute in this case, and this Court confirms this.

Pursuant to Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law, a third-party revocation action must satisfy the following conditions: first, as to subject, it can only be a third party who, as provided respectively in paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law, has an independent claim to the subject matter in dispute between the parties, or who, though having no independent claim, has a legal interest in the outcome of the case; second, as to substance, there is evidence that the contents of the effective judgment, ruling, or consent judgment are erroneous in whole or in part, harming the civil rights and interests of the third party; third, as to procedure, the third party failed to participate in the litigation due to reasons not attributable to itself, and files the action with the people's court that rendered the effective judgment, ruling, or consent judgment within six months from the date it knew or should have known that its civil rights and interests were harmed. Focusing on the reasons for the court of first instance's ruling to dismiss the complaint, the issues in dispute between the parties in the second instance are: whether Yancheng Company has the subject qualification to bring this action, whether there is evidence that the creditor's rights confirmed by Civil Mediation Document No. 2 are fraudulent, whether Yancheng Company's action was filed beyond the statutory time limit, and whether there were procedural errors in the trial of this case by the court of first instance.

The purpose of the third-party revocation action system established by the Civil Procedure Law is to protect the rights and interests of third parties harmed by erroneous effective judgments, especially those harmed by fraudulent litigation, so that a third party who did not participate in the litigation due to reasons not attributable to itself may file an action with the people's court for relief. Therefore, whether Yancheng Company qualifies as a third party under Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law determines whether it has the subject qualification to bring this action. From the facts it asserts, Yancheng Company did not bring this action as a third party with an independent claim, but rather alleged that the relevant parties maliciously colluded to engage in fraudulent litigation harming its creditor's rights as the ground for its action. Obviously, whether Yancheng Company falls within the category of a third party without an independent claim is the fundamental starting point for determining the issue in this case.

Under paragraph 2 of Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law, a third party who has no independent claim to the subject matter in dispute between the parties but has a legal interest in the outcome of the case is a third party without an independent claim. Thus, having a legal interest is the essential element for a third party without an independent claim. Yancheng Company filed this action with the people's court seeking protection of its civil rights, which are creditor's rights. Given the relative nature of creditor's rights, in general, a third party who is an ordinary creditor does not have grounds for bringing a third-party revocation action based on its creditor's rights. However, under paragraph 1 of Article 74 of the Contract Law of the PRC (hereinafter "Contract Law"), if a debtor waives a matured claim or transfers property without consideration, thereby harming the creditor, the creditor may request the people's court to revoke the debtor's act; if the debtor transfers property at a price obviously unreasonably low, thereby harming the creditor, and the transferee knows of the circumstances, the creditor may also request the people's court to revoke the debtor's act. Accordingly, if the debtor's property disposal acts as confirmed by the effective judgment satisfy the conditions for the right of revocation under Article 74 of the Contract Law, then the creditor who enjoys the right of revocation has a legal interest in the outcome of the case of that effective judgment, and thus has the plaintiff's subject qualification to bring a third-party revocation action as a third party without an independent claim.

In this case, the evidence presented by Yancheng Company shows that the Fujian Provincial People's Procuratorate had issued the "Procuratorial Suggestion Letter" Min Jian Jian (2003) No. 2 on August 19, 2003, suggesting that the Fujian High People's Court retry Case No. 2 according to law. The Fujian High People's Court issued the "Letter for Transfer of Criminal Clues" (2003) Min Min Jian Zi No. 149 on October 24, 2003, stating that Zheng Yaonan and Zhang Qiongyue were suspected of malicious collusion to misappropriate the property of Far East Xiamen Company, thereby harming the legitimate rights and interests of Hong Kong Far East Company, and accordingly transferred the relevant criminal clues to the Fujian Provincial Public Security Department for investigation. Therefore, Yancheng Company has provided corresponding evidence that Case No. 2 was a fraudulent litigation and that the creditor's rights confirmed by Civil Mediation Document No. 2 were fraudulent. The situation it alleges, that Far East Xiamen Company admitted Zheng Yaonan's fraudulent creditor's rights by entering into a mediation agreement in civil proceedings and formulating a repayment plan, falls within the category of transferring property without consideration harming the interests of creditors under paragraph 1 of Article 74 of the Contract Law. Yancheng Company has a legal interest in the outcome of Case No. 2, especially when Far East Xiamen Company has been declared bankrupt by the people's court and its property is insufficient to pay all its debts, Yancheng Company's creditor's rights will inevitably be directly affected by the existence and amount of Zheng Yaonan's creditor's rights. As a creditor of Far East Xiamen Company, Yancheng Company enjoys the right of revocation under Article 74 of the Contract Law and has the subject qualification to bring this third-party revocation action.

Pursuant to paragraph 3 of Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law, a third party "may file an action with the people's court within six months from the date it knew or should have known that its civil rights and interests were harmed." The starting point of this six-month period for filing is the date the party knew or should have known that its civil rights and interests were harmed. In this case, when Far East Xiamen Company had sufficient assets to pay all its debts, Civil Mediation Document No. 2 had no impact on the realization of Yancheng Company's creditor's rights; when Far East Company operated normally, it was also difficult to determine that Civil Mediation Document No. 2 would harm Yancheng Company's creditor's rights. However, when Far East Xiamen Company entered bankruptcy proceedings due to inability to pay all its debts in full, Yancheng Company and Gao Lizhen, the assignee of Zheng Yaonan's creditor's rights, are both bankruptcy creditors, and Gao Lizhen declared creditor's rights based on Civil Mediation Document No. 2, the degree of realization of Yancheng Company's bankruptcy creditor's rights would be harmed by Civil Mediation Document No. 2 underlying Gao Lizhen's bankruptcy creditor's rights. Therefore, it should be held that Yancheng Company knew or should have known that its civil rights and interests were harmed only after it learned of the information that Far East Xiamen Company had entered bankruptcy proceedings. The "Notice Regarding the Bankruptcy Case of Far East (Xiamen) Real Estate Development Co., Ltd." presented by Yancheng Company shows that Yancheng Company signed for the materials regarding creditor's rights declarations prepared by the bankruptcy administrator on March 15, 2016, and it filed a complaint with the Fujian High People's Court on September 12, 2016, requesting revocation of Civil Mediation Document No. 2, which did not exceed the six-month period for filing. Although Lei Yuansi, then general manager of Yancheng Company, had filed an appeal with the Fujian High People's Court and the Fujian Provincial People's Procuratorate in July 2003 regarding Case No. 2, he did so in his capacity as a shareholder and director of Hong Kong Far East Company and director and general manager of Far East Xiamen Company to protect the interests of Far East Xiamen Company, not Yancheng Company's creditor's rights. Moreover, at that time, whether Yancheng Company suffered harm due to Civil Mediation Document No. 2 was uncertain, so there was no issue of whether it knew or should have known, and consequently no issue of starting the six-month period under paragraph 3 of Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law. The arguments of Zheng Yaonan and Gao Lizhen that Yancheng Company had exceeded the statutory time limit when it filed this action lack sufficient basis. The determination of the court of first instance on this issue is erroneous and should be corrected. In addition, although the creditor's rights under Civil Mediation Document No. 2 have been assigned to Gao Lizhen, because those creditor's rights are suspected of arising from fraudulent litigation, Zheng Yaonan, as the creditor who initiated the litigation in Case No. 2, should participate in this action as a defendant in the third-party revocation action according to law. Zheng Yaonan's argument that the creditor's rights under the mediation document involved have been lawfully assigned and that this case is unrelated to him cannot stand.

Given that a third-party revocation action involves a determination of an effective judgment and concerns the rights and obligations of the parties to the original effective judgment and the third party, Article 294 of the Judicial Interpretation of the Civil Procedure Law specifically provides: "In a third-party revocation action case, the people's court shall form a collegial panel and hold a hearing." Accordingly, after a third-party revocation action is docketed, written proceedings are not applicable, and the court receiving the case shall form a collegial panel and hold a hearing. If the opposing party raises objections to the third party's litigation subject qualification or other conditions for filing the action, it must also be determined after a hearing by the collegial panel according to law. After receiving this case, the court of first instance dismissed Yancheng Company's complaint without holding a hearing according to law. This procedural error should be corrected.

In summary, Yancheng Company's filing of this third-party revocation action satisfies the conditions for filing an action under Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC. The court of first instance's ruling to dismiss its complaint is an improper application of law. The grounds of appeal of Yancheng Company are established, and this Court supports them. In accordance with Article 171 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 332 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the ruling is as follows:

1. Revoke the civil ruling (2016) Min Min Che Zi No. 6 of the Fujian High People's Court;

2. Order the Fujian High People's Court to retry this case.

This ruling is final.
